text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The decision by the Moslem Brotherhood to boycott November parliamentary elections has opened new possibilities in the political game; head of the movement says the movement is targeted by the state and the head of its political arm says "ball is in the government's court."

- The possibility of extending parliament is now a possibility after the decision by the Moslem Brotherhood to boycott next parliamentary elections; other opposition parties to discuss their position in a emergency meeting on Thursday.
- Moslem Brotherhood place six conditions to go back on their decision to boycott the 1997 elections.
- EU (European Union) pledges support to Jordan in its economic reform programme.
- Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali says "everyone is free in either particpating in the election or boycotting it."
- Arab Bank stock rises to its highest level since February 1991.
- Appeals court drops all charges against honorary consul of Sri Lanka in alleged baby sale case.
- Islamic Action Front and other parties study option to follow Brotherhood's decision.
